title: DS block / page-template registry entry (PROPOSED — gate 0/1 spec, not yet read by any tooling)
description: A block is a composition of registry components with a named layout frame; a template is a full page composed of blocks. Neither introduces a new interactive primitive or a new visual treatment: everything a reader sees comes from a component, and everything between components comes from a --rata-* layout token. Modelled on registry/schema.json — the same written/derived split applies once a block is implemented (see docs/blocks/README.md).

name.description: kebab-case id, doubles as docs slug and CLI arg. Must not collide with a component name in registry/components/ — `rata add <name>` resolves both namespaces.

kind.description: `block`: one region-sized composition placed inside a page (a hero, a sign-in form). `template`: a whole page — it owns the <main>, the single <h1>, the skip link and the shell; it composes blocks and components but never restyles them.

surface.description: Where the block is meant to appear. `website` = public marketing pages; `web-app` = signed-in product UI in a browser; `native-app` = an iOS/Android app. A block listing `native-app` must give a non-trivial `native.mapping`.

category.description: Docs IA grouping, the block equivalent of a component's `family`.

alsoKnownAs.description: Names people search for, so `rata list` and agents find the block under any of them.

status.description: Per-artifact lifecycle. `layout` is the block's own CSS — layout only (grid, gaps, region widths), never colour or type, which belong to the components inside it.

precedent.description: The existing page shell this block's frame follows (a path under apps/), or the word `none` with the reason in behavior.decisions. Frame-first: find the precedent before inventing a shell.

frame.description: The frame-first decision, made before any content: which shell, and which container the content type calls for (CLAUDE.md, Frame-first layout).

shell.description: The arrangement of the regions. `stacked` = regions one above the other at every width; `split` = two panes side by side that stack when narrow.

container.description: Per CLAUDE.md: dense scannable rows → table/list; widgets, galleries, settings groups → card; everything else → plain section. `card` and `table` are future components today and must also appear in dependsOnFuture.

regions.description: Named layout regions, in source order. Budgets are stated per breakpoint CLASS (narrow/medium/wide), not per pixel value — the system has no breakpoint tokens, and the values behind the classes are an open decision (docs/blocks/README.md, Token gaps).

element.description: The HTML element or component that renders the region (`section`, `header`, `nav`, `aside`, `ul`, `footer`, `TopNav`, …).

contains.description: Registry component names (or block names, for a template) rendered inside this region.

budget.description: Inline-size budget per breakpoint class, written as a token expression (`fill`, `calc(var(--rata-size-control-lg) * 6)`, `1fr of 3`, `hidden`). Never a bare px value.

collapse.description: What happens to this region as space runs out: stacks, hides behind a trigger, becomes a Sheet, scrolls, etc.

components.description: Every registry component the block renders. Each `name` must exist in registry/components/ (proposed build check). A component whose status.react is `future` must also be listed in dependsOnFuture.

for.description: What this component does in this block.

region.description: Which region it lives in; must match a regions[].name.

blocks.description: Templates only: the blocks this template composes, by registry/blocks name, in page order.

headingLevel.description: The headingLevel the template passes this block — templates own the outline.

dependsOnFuture.description: Components this block needs that are `future` (contract approved or proposed, no code). The block cannot leave `future` until every `blocking: true` entry is `latest`.

via.description: Templates only: the block (or comma-separated blocks) through which this dependency arrives, when the template does not render the component directly. A template inherits every blocking dependency of its required blocks.

blocking.description: true: the block cannot ship without it. false: the block ships without that part and adds it when the component lands.

interim.description: What the block does until the component ships, when blocking is false. Never a hand-rolled stand-in (no <div className="card">).

slots.description: The block's content API — the written contract for each slot, same shape as a component prop entry. Spec mode: type/required are written by hand while status.react is `future`; once implemented they are derived from packages/blocks/src/<name>.tsx and must be deleted here.

decisions.description: Decisions worth defending, each with its reason — the record of what is being approved at gate 1.

landmarks.description: Landmarks the block or template renders. A block renders at most a labelled region (`section` with aria-labelledby) and never a <main>; only a template renders <main>.

label.description: How the landmark is named (aria-labelledby target or aria-label text).

headingOutline.description: The headings the block produces, in order. `level` is relative to the block's required headingLevel slot (`base`, `base+1`) for a block, and absolute (1–6) for a template.

repeats.description: One per item (a feature, a plan, a question).

obligations.description: What the caller must do that the block cannot do for them.

strategy.description: `intrinsic`: the layout reflows by itself (auto-fill grid with a token-derived minimum, flex-wrap) and needs no breakpoint — the playground gallery's precedent and the preferred answer. `container-query`: reacts to the block's own width, so it behaves the same inside a sidebar layout and full-width. `media-query`: only for templates, which own the viewport.

reason.description: Why it does or does not apply — required when applies is false.

mapping.description: How the block's regions map to platform structures (navigation stack, grouped list, tab bar, sheet).

tokens.description: The block's LAYOUT recipe only: region gaps, padding, grid minimums, band backgrounds. Every value is a token path or a calc over one. Colour and type of anything inside the block belong to the component that renders it, never here.

tokenGaps.description: Layout values this block needs that no token provides today. Stated as a need, never as an invented token name — a new token goes through the design-tokens skill's Gate 1/2/3.

interim.description: What the spec does meanwhile (usually a calc over size.control.*, the system's existing derivation habit).

usage.description: Worked cases. Examples are linted against the token rules by internal/vibe-tests (proposed: same as component usage).

openQuestions.description: Decisions the gate-1 reviewer must make before this block can move on.
